question: What is the main purpose of CCTV inspection in a sanitary sewer?
correctAnswer: To view and record the inside condition of the pipe without excavation
explanation: A CCTV camera travels through the pipe so staff can see and record its condition and defects, which supports cleaning, repair, and rehabilitation planning without digging.
options: To clean grease from the pipe walls
To view and record the inside condition of the pipe without excavation
To measure the exact flow rate in the sewer
To repair cracks found in the pipe
optionA: To clean grease from the pipe walls
optionB: To view and record the inside condition of the pipe without excavation
optionC: To measure the exact flow rate in the sewer
optionD: To repair cracks found in the pipe
sourceTitle: US EPA — CMOM Guide for Sanitary Sewer Collection Systems

question: Why is a sewer usually cleaned before a CCTV inspection?

explanation: A camera can only record what it can see. Removing deposits and debris first gives a clear view of cracks, joints, roots, and other defects.
options: Debris and grease on the pipe walls can hide defects from the camera
Cleaning raises the flow so the camera travels faster
Cleaning lets the camera float through the pipe on the surface
Cleaning removes the need for a traffic control plan
optionA: Debris and grease on the pipe walls can hide defects from the camera
optionB: Cleaning raises the flow so the camera travels faster
optionC: Cleaning lets the camera float through the pipe on the surface
optionD: Cleaning removes the need for a traffic control plan

The pipe is too clean for the camera to grip
The sewer flows in the wrong direction
The manhole cover was left open during the inspection
optionA: Heavy debris, roots, or a collapsed section blocks the camera path
optionB: The pipe is too clean for the camera to grip
optionC: The sewer flows in the wrong direction
optionD: The manhole cover was left open during the inspection

question: What does FOG stand for in wastewater collection work?

explanation: FOG is the fats, oils, and grease that enter sewers from kitchens and food premises and build up inside pipes.

Fats, odours, and gases
Fats, oils, and grease
Fine organic grit

question: How do tree roots most often enter a sewer pipe?
correctAnswer: Through cracked joints, defective connections, and other openings in the pipe
explanation: Roots seek moisture and nutrients. They enter through small cracks, open joints, and defective service connections, then grow inside the pipe.
options: Through cracked joints, defective connections, and other openings in the pipe
Through the treatment plant outfall
Through open manhole covers
Through household water softeners
optionA: Through cracked joints, defective connections, and other openings in the pipe
optionB: Through the treatment plant outfall
optionC: Through open manhole covers
optionD: Through household water softeners

question: Why does FOG cause blockages as it moves through a sewer?
correctAnswer: It cools, sticks to the pipe walls, and builds up until the flow is restricted
explanation: Warm grease from kitchens cools in the sewer, coats the walls, and traps solids. The opening narrows over time until a blockage forms.
options: It dissolves the pipe from the inside
It cools, sticks to the pipe walls, and builds up until the flow is restricted
It evaporates and leaves the pipe dry
It makes the wastewater flow too fast to carry solids
optionA: It dissolves the pipe from the inside
optionB: It cools, sticks to the pipe walls, and builds up until the flow is restricted
optionC: It evaporates and leaves the pipe dry
optionD: It makes the wastewater flow too fast to carry solids

question: Which item is a common cause of sewer blockages even though it is sold as flushable?
correctAnswer: Disposable wipes that do not break down in the sewer
explanation: Wipes stay intact in wastewater, snag on rough spots and roots, and collect into masses that block pipes and pumps.
options: Disposable wipes that do not break down in the sewer
Toilet paper that breaks apart quickly in water
Dissolved soap from a dishwasher
Rainwater entering through a roof leader
optionA: Disposable wipes that do not break down in the sewer
optionB: Toilet paper that breaks apart quickly in water
optionC: Dissolved soap from a dishwasher
optionD: Rainwater entering through a roof leader

correctAnswer: They grow thicker and catch grease and solids, narrowing the pipe
explanation: Root masses thicken over time and act like a net, trapping FOG and debris until flow is restricted or blocked.

They seal cracks and stop infiltration
They dissolve as soon as wastewater covers them
They grow thicker and catch grease and solids, narrowing the pipe
optionA: They grow back out through the same joint only
optionB: They seal cracks and stop infiltration

question: Why should an operator never rely on smell alone to judge whether hydrogen sulfide is at a safe level?
correctAnswer: Hydrogen sulfide can deaden the sense of smell, so a fading odour does not mean the gas is gone
explanation: Hydrogen sulfide causes olfactory fatigue. The odour can seem to fade while the gas is still present at dangerous levels, so a calibrated detector must be used.
options: The smell gets stronger as the gas gets weaker
Hydrogen sulfide can deaden the sense of smell, so a fading odour does not mean the gas is gone
Hydrogen sulfide has no effect on workers
Smell is the approved method for gas testing
optionA: The smell gets stronger as the gas gets weaker
optionB: Hydrogen sulfide can deaden the sense of smell, so a fading odour does not mean the gas is gone
optionC: Hydrogen sulfide has no effect on workers
optionD: Smell is the approved method for gas testing

correctAnswer: In low, poorly ventilated spaces such as wet wells and deep manholes
explanation: Hydrogen sulfide is heavier than air and collects in low, still spaces below grade, which is why wet wells and manholes are high risk locations.
options: Only at the surface of open channels
In high areas well above the wastewater
In low, poorly ventilated spaces such as wet wells and deep manholes
Only inside pressurized drinking water mains
optionA: Only at the surface of open channels
optionB: In high areas well above the wastewater
optionC: In low, poorly ventilated spaces such as wet wells and deep manholes
optionD: Only inside pressurized drinking water mains

correctAnswer: Wastewater held in the force main can turn septic and release hydrogen sulfide when it discharges
explanation: Long detention in a full force main lets wastewater turn septic. When it discharges and becomes turbulent at the manhole, dissolved hydrogen sulfide is released to the air.

The manhole cover is the wrong colour
Force mains add oxygen that creates odour
Odour at a manhole only ever comes from the storm sewer
optionA: Wastewater held in the force main can turn septic and release hydrogen sulfide when it discharges
optionB: The manhole cover is the wrong colour
optionC: Force mains add oxygen that creates odour
optionD: Odour at a manhole only ever comes from the storm sewer

correctAnswer: Do not enter, withdraw from the opening, and follow the ventilation and confined space procedure before any entry is considered

Complete the inspection from the bottom since the crew is already on site
Ignore the alarm because the inspection started from the surface

question: Why is an open manhole never left unguarded, even during a short break?

An open hole lets odours out of the sewer
